## Course Description

Fundamental concepts, techniques, and applications of risk assessment and risk management for engineering systems; current industry practices for risk assessment of industrial facilities using qualitative and quantitative approaches are demonstrated through exercises and case studies from diverse engineering fields.

## Special Course Designation

None

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- Comprehend and articulate the fundamental goals and methodologies of the Systems Engineering discipline.

- Operate proficiently with international standards governing Systems Engineering and Risk Management.

- Conduct a comprehensive risk analysis, including the identification and assessment of potential hazards, to develop effective mitigation strategies.

- Develop and interpret probabilistic risk assessments for intricate engineering systems.

- Evaluate and model the reliability of individual engineering components and complex, interconnected systems.

## Textbook and/or Resource Materials

## Grading Policy

Quizzes, homework, assignments (20%)

Unit 1 Evaluation: Systems Engineering (20%)

Unit 2 Evaluation: Risk Management (20%)

Unit 3 Evaluation: Probabilistic Risk Assessment - PRA (10%)

Unit 4 Evaluation: Reliability (30%)

[90%,100%] gets an A, [80%,90%) gets a B, [70%,80%) gets a C, [60%, 70%) gets a D, and less than 60% gets an F.

Major evaluations will be administered at the end of each module. Minor tests and homework will be given throughout the module. Minor assessment will account for no more than 33% of the module's weight.

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).

## Course Specific Late Work Policy

No late work will be accepted.

## Additional Course Information

### Scientific Software

MATLAB, R, Excel, or Python might also be used for classwork and homework.

### Course Format

- Online lectures with exercises, quizzes, and evaluations.

- Read the assigned material, including examples, and try to solve the exercises in the handouts.

- Watch the video lectures.

- Review class exercises; optionally, complement your preparation by working with the suggested textbooks.

- Use the instructor's office hours.

- Turn in quizzes; if anything is unclear, make a note of each. Partial credit will be given when possible.

- To contest a grade, please submit a formal written objection within three days of the graded evaluation's due date.

- If necessary, tests and exams might be regraded to ensure the integrity and accuracy of the questions. Some students' grades may decrease after the regrading.

### Communications

To maintain course integrity, all communications must be conducted through Canvas (via a message). The instructor will not respond to course-related questions via email or chat.

### How to Succeed in the Course?

- Read and abide by the Aggie Code of Honor

- Be respectful of your peers and instructor.

- Plan to spend 12 hours on the course each week, including time needed to watch the video lectures.

- Do not put things off to the last minute; this course needs extreme diligence.

- Ask questions using Canvas.

- Solve the exercise problems on your own before looking at the solution (when applicable).

- If something is not clear, ask questions during office hours (ask for help as early as possible).

- Attempt all the exercise problems before coming to class.

- Prepare extremely well for quizzes and exams.

- For the math-based units or modules, the procedure to obtain an answer is as valid as the answer itself.
